reasoning: A wins, but only narrowly. Both attempts add the same correct model.json and both pass every check. Their server and client logic is nearly the same, including the GetPlayers loop, the StarterKitGiven attribute and the SetCore retries in pcall. The deciding difference is that A loads BlockTypes on the client with WaitForChild, as the rubric asks. B indexes ReplicatedStorage.Shared.BlockTypes directly, which can fail if replication is late. A also warns when an attribute is missing and won't give the kit twice. B's clamping and its skip of the empty-kit notification are nice touches, but they don't make up for the unguarded require.

criteria.note: src/ReplicatedStorage/Shared/StarterKit.model.json with className Configuration and attributes, under the mounted Shared path.
Brick 20, Dirt 20, Grass 10, Window 0, Wood 10 are all unquoted numbers.
Edits Main.server.luau in ServerScriptService and Main.client.luau in StarterPlayerScripts, and adds no misplaced modules.

criteria.criterion: Reads StarterKit at the right path and covers every type
criteria.note: The server waits for ReplicatedStorage.Shared:WaitForChild("StarterKit") and loops over BlockTypes.List, warning and using 0 when an attribute isn't a number; the client loads BlockTypes through WaitForChild("Shared"):WaitForChild("BlockTypes").

criteria.criterion: Existing players, one-time notification, SetCore guard
criteria.note: Loops over Players:GetPlayers() with task.spawn, waits for the StarterKitGiven attribute before notifying once, and wraps SetCore in pcall with up to 20 retries at 0.5 s.
Every check passes and the diff only touches kit-related code.
Same StarterKit.model.json under src/ReplicatedStorage/Shared with className Configuration.
All five counts are JSON numbers.
Main.server.luau sits in ServerScriptService and Main.client.luau in StarterPlayerScripts.

criteria.criterion: Reads StarterKit at the right path and covers every type
criteria.note: The server uses Shared:WaitForChild("StarterKit") and getStarterCount over BlockTypes.List, using 0 for a missing attribute; but the client requires ReplicatedStorage.Shared.BlockTypes directly with no WaitForChild.

criteria.criterion: Existing players, one-time notification, SetCore guard
criteria.note: Has the GetPlayers loop, and its connection disconnects after the first truthy StarterKitGiven so it fires once; pcall(StarterGui.SetCore, ...) retries 20 times.
Every check passes and there are no unrelated edits.

strengths: Uses WaitForChild on the client to load Shared/BlockTypes, so it doesn't depend on replication order
A StarterKitGiven guard keeps the kit from being given twice if PlayerAdded and the GetPlayers loop both reach the same player
Retries SetCore inside pcall and waits for a single completion attribute before notifying
weaknesses: Shows a notification saying "No blocks this time." even when every count is 0, which is minor
The attribute name is duplicated across server and client instead of living in a shared module

strengths: Clamps and floors counts, and warns when an attribute has the wrong type
Disconnects its connection cleanly after notifying once, and skips the notification when the kit is empty
weaknesses: The client requires ReplicatedStorage.Shared.BlockTypes without WaitForChild, which can fail if replication is late
Has no guard against giving the kit twice (harmless, since it writes the same values)
Says nothing when an attribute is missing, so a designer could delete one without noticing
